name: Völkisch nationalism
summary: Völkisch nationalism was the radical ethnic-nationalist movement and worldview of the German-speaking lands from the 1880s to 1933. It made race, descent and rootedness in the land the basis of the Volk, saw Jews as the chief enemy, rejected democracy, liberalism, socialism and everything international, and sought a homogeneous, hierarchical national community and a larger Germanic Reich.
scope: The movement of the Kaiserreich and Weimar Republic as documented by the scholarship (Puschner, Maleszka) and its theorists (Chamberlain, Lagarde, Heinrich Class). It never agreed on one manifesto; answers rest on what the scholarship says the movement as a whole held and on the writers read. Splits between pagan and German-Christian wings, and between monarchist and non-monarchist views, are left unanswered or marked mixed. Nazism has its own entry and is not used.
